added_models.model: Pancreatic duct-ligated dogs (Mayo Clinic, DiMagno), dosed with Burkholderia plantarii bacterial lipase

efficacy.note: B. plantarii lipase cut steatorrhea dose-dependently in duct-ligated dogs; liquid beat powder; authors predicted it may abolish human steatorrhea.
efficacy.quote: The combination of adequate mixing of small amounts (milligrams) of bacterial lipase and high-fat meals abolishes canine steatorrhea and may abolish human pancreatic steatorrhea.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract plus full-text methods (scraped PDF): lipase was B. plantarii lipase from Knoll AG, the enzyme later developed as burlulipase; not the NM-BL liquid formulation itself.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry. The dog enzyme is the same bacterial lipase (B. plantarii) that became burlulipase, so product_in_model true at medium confidence; the dog readout is CFA, the human primary endpoint.

efficacy.note: Phase 2a crossover in CF-EPI (NCT01710644): CFA 72.7% on burlulipase (NM-BL, liquid) vs 53.8% on placebo, as the dogs predicted in direction.
efficacy.short: CFA rose vs placebo in CF patients
efficacy.quote: During treatment with NM-BL, the coefficient of fat absorption was significantly greater (72.7%) compared with placebo (53.8%) with a difference between groups of 18.8% (P < .001).
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (Europe PMC); full text blocked. Registry NCT01710644 (first posted 2012-10-19) has no posted results.
efficacy.reason: Burlulipase raised CFA as dogs predicted
efficacy.judgement: Paired by me; the trial abstract does not cite the dog work. Direction matched, but the dogs' near-abolition of steatorrhea was not reproduced (72.7% CFA is far from normal), so magnitude is direction_only. CF-EPI counts as the EPI disease, as in the draft.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: CFA: dogs near-normal at 300,000-600,000 IU (240 mg); patients 72.7% vs 53.8% placebo

considered_not_added: Ex-vivo human gastric/duodenal juice survival assay (Raimondo & DiMagno 1994, B. plantarii vs porcine lipase): predicted bacterial lipase would be more effective than porcine lipase; no head-to-head burlulipase vs porcine PERT trial was found (Heubi 2016 was placebo-controlled), so no patient comparison.

In-vitro test-meal assay for YLLIP2 (Aloulou 2015: 10 mg = 1200 mg pancreatin): a potency ratio, not a human regimen; MS1819-SD lipase content in the 2.2 g/d clinical dose is undisclosed, so no admissible comparison (the draft already folds it into the minipig dose entry).
Duct-ligated dog dose statement (Suzuki 1997: 300,000-600,000 IU = 120-240 mg in humans): the NM-BL dose in Heubi 2016 could not be read (full text blocked), so no dose-cell comparison was entered.
Suzuki 1999 dog finding that porcine lipase gave more fat absorption than bacterial lipase on a standard diet: no burlulipase vs PERT patient trial found to compare it with.
SLV339 (Solvay): no published preclinical or disease-model data found; dose-ranging trial in chronic pancreatitis has no public results.
Patient-derived cells/organoids, PDX, human genetic or in-silico/QSP models: none found for any member; not applicable to an oral lumen-acting enzyme.
